The Optical Recognition of Handwritten Digits data [@alpaydin1998optdigits]
are scans of digits written by hand on forms.
Each scan was reduced to an 8 by 8 grid of pixels,
and each pixel counts how many of the 16 dots in its 4 by 4 block of a 32 by 32 bitmap of the scan were inked,
so it holds a whole number from 0 to 16.
The [UCI Machine Learning Repository](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/80) publishes the data
under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license.

[`data/optdigits-test.csv`](data/optdigits-test.csv) is a copy of its test file, `optdigits.tes`,
byte for byte, under a new name.
Each row is one image:
64 pixel values, read across the rows of the grid from top left to bottom right,
then the digit the writer meant, 0 to 9.
The file has no header row.
